feature: How the words of a caption show
summary: Captions can show a sentence, a line, 3, 2 or 1 word at a time, and the word being said can have its own colour, pill, glow, stroke, shadow and size, with a Grow, a soft bounce, a Pop or an underline sweep. Five style tiles play the real caption and set all of it in one click, and your own tweak can be saved as a style.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open a screen recording with somebody talking; the captions write themselves.

try.do: Click Captions in the layers list and scroll the panel to Caption style.
Set Show to 1 word, Animation to Grow with bounce, and the Current word Glow to Yellow.
Press space and watch each word land with a soft spring and a glow of its own.
Drag Scale and Speed under Current word until it feels right, then click Save style.
Set Coming to Hidden and play: the words appear as they are said.
Export the film and compare a popping word with the canvas.

evaluate: Is the Grow with bounce soft enough, or does it read as a jolt at the default speed?
Do the five tiles make it quicker to get a good look than CapCut or Submagic?
Is 3 words the right default for Bold pop, or should it be 2?
Is Current word the right place for the pop controls, or should they sit above Show?
Would you rather Show changes stay out of the timeline (the bars stay as lines) instead of re-splitting it into many small bars?
rough: The mock (video-captions.html) draws a three-way segmented style bar and a line of copy about the design system; the task asked for preview tiles, so tiles replace the bar and that line is not shipped, since there is no design-system link for it to be true about.
The Captions section is long now and sits below Time in the panel, so reaching the style tiles takes a scroll.
Picking Show re-splits the captions on the timeline (1 word gives one bar per word, the way CapCut does); captions you retimed by hand are re-derived from their words' times.

While a look makes the current word grow, the line sits a little higher in its box so the grown word and its glow are not cut off at the bottom. Double-click word fixing measures the unlifted line, so it can be off by a few points.
A popping caption costs about 4 ms to draw at 1080p on this machine (measured in the test suite). A full-length export was not timed frame by frame.
